title: Linux Foundation Announces the Formation of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), Anchored by New Project Contributions Including Model Context Protocol (MCP), goose and AGENTS.md
summary: The Linux Foundation launched the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) as a neutral home for open agentic AI projects, seeded with three contributions: Anthropic's Model Context Protocol, Block's goose agent framework and OpenAI's AGENTS.md. Platinum members at launch were AWS, Anthropic, Block, Bloomberg, Cloudflare, Google, Microsoft and OpenAI, with 18 Gold members (including Cisco, IBM, Okta, Salesforce, SAP, Temporal) and 23 Silver members.
relevance: Places the dominant agent-to-tool protocol under vendor-neutral governance, which shapes how any portable task envelope or handoff standard can be stewarded.
search_query: Linux Foundation Agentic AI Foundation AAIF announcement

title: Agentic AI Foundation Welcomes 97 New Members As Demand for Open, Collaborative Agent Standardization Increases
summary: Announced at the Linux Foundation Member Summit in Napa, AAIF added 97 members (18 Gold, 79 Silver), bringing its total to 146. New Gold members included American Express, JPMorgan Chase, Red Hat, ServiceNow, UiPath and Huawei, and AWS's David Nalley was appointed chair of the governing board.
relevance: Shows how quickly enterprises are consolidating agent-standard governance in one foundation, a precondition for cross-organization agent movement standards.
search_query: Agentic AI Foundation new members projects 2026 joins AAIF

title: agentgateway Joins AAIF as an Open Gateway for Agentic AI Infrastructure
summary: AAIF accepted agentgateway, a Rust-based, Apache-2.0 proxy and control plane for MCP, A2A, LLM, HTTP and gRPC traffic originally led by Solo.io, as its fourth hosted project. The post lists features including MCP server federation with tool-level policies, JWT/API-key auth, RBAC, mTLS and external authorization, and says the project has 300+ contributors from 60+ organizations.
relevance: A neutral gateway that mediates both agent-to-tool and agent-to-agent traffic is a natural enforcement and audit point for delegated or relocated agent tasks.
search_query: agentgateway contributed Agentic AI Foundation project announcement

title: Agentic AI Foundation Welcomes 57 New Members, Gaining Major Financial Services Players and APAC Leaders
summary: Datelined Seoul, AAIF reported 57 new members (3 Gold, 33 Silver, 21 Associate), for a total of 247; Alibaba, Visa and Wells Fargo joined as Gold members and Stanford, CERN and ETRI among Associates. The release cites AAIF's Agentic AI Momentum Report, which it says tracks 116 open source projects across five layers of the agentic stack, and lists MCP, goose, AGENTS.md and agentgateway as foundation projects.
relevance: Documents the widening (financial, APAC, academic) constituency behind AAIF governance and an ecosystem-mapping report useful for positioning agent-movement layers.
search_query: "Agentic AI Foundation" welcomes 57 new members August 2026
notes: AAIF's own news page dates the same release 2026-08-12; the LF press page dateline is 2026-08-13. Release states 21 Associate members but names 20.

title: A2A joins AAIF's open agentic stack
summary: AAIF announced that the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol joins as a hosted project, placing agent-to-agent and agent-to-tool protocols under the same foundation. The post recaps that A2A v1.0 shipped in March 2026 with multi-protocol bindings, version negotiation, multi-tenancy and signed agent cards, that IBM's Agent Communication Protocol merged into A2A in August 2025, and that over 150 organizations back the protocol.
relevance: Co-governance of A2A (delegation) and MCP (tool access) in one body is the governance event most directly relevant to standardizing agent handoff and a shared task context.
search_query: aaif.io A2A Agent2Agent hosted project Agentic AI Foundation announcement
notes: Governance move, not the A2A launch. Secondary coverage: Techzine, 'Google transfers A2A to the Agentic AI Foundation' (2026-08-17, Berry Zwets), https://www.techzine.eu/news/devops/143659/google-transfers-a2a-to-the-agentic-ai-foundation/ . Deployment claims are AAIF-reported.

title: Linux Foundation Welcomes the AGNTCY Project to Standardize Open Multi-Agent System Infrastructure and Break Down AI Agent Silos
summary: The Linux Foundation took over governance of AGNTCY, infrastructure for agent discovery (Open Agent Schema Framework), verifiable agent identity, messaging (SLIM) and multi-agent observability that Cisco open-sourced in March 2025 with LangChain and Galileo. Cisco, Dell, Google Cloud, Oracle and Red Hat joined as formative members, and the LF says 65+ companies support it and that it interoperates with A2A and MCP.
relevance: AGNTCY bundles discovery, identity, transport and observability, the cross-cutting layers an agent needs to move between vendors and frameworks.
search_query: AGNTCY joins Linux Foundation Cisco agent interoperability

title: Announcing the "AI Agent Standards Initiative" for Interoperable and Secure Innovation
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
summary: NIST's Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI), with NIST's Information Technology Laboratory and the National Science Foundation, launched an AI Agent Standards Initiative. It rests on three pillars: industry-led agent standards with U.S. participation in international bodies, community-led open-source agent protocols, and research on agent security and identity, with comment deadlines of March 9 (security RFI) and April 2, 2026 (identity concept paper).
relevance: A national standards body explicitly targeting agent interoperability and identity sets the policy frame in which handoff and relocation protocols will be judged.
search_query: NIST CAISI AI Agent Standards Initiative announcement
notes: Page last updated 2026-02-18; some secondary outlets date the announcement 2026-02-20.

title: CAISI Issues Request for Information About Securing AI Agent Systems
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
summary: CAISI requested public input on secure development and deployment of AI agent systems, focusing on risks such as indirect prompt injection, data poisoning and models acting against security without adversarial input. It asked about threats, mitigations, measurement and deployment-environment controls that limit and monitor agent access; comments were due March 9, 2026 under docket NIST-2025-0035.
relevance: Signals that monitoring and constraining agent access in the deployment environment is expected to become formal guidance, affecting how relocated agents must be sandboxed and audited.
search_query: CAISI request for information AI agent security Federal Register January 2026

title: New Concept Paper on Identity and Authority of Software Agents
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) / NCCoE
summary: NIST's National Cybersecurity Center of Excellence released a concept paper, 'Accelerating the Adoption of Software and AI Agent Identity and Authorization', scoping a possible project to apply existing identity standards to agentic AI. It sought feedback on use cases, standards and controls for identification, authorization, auditing, non-repudiation and prompt-injection mitigation, with comments open until April 2, 2026.
relevance: Agent identity and authorization across delegation hops is a core requirement for accountable task handoff between agents and organizations.
search_query: NCCoE AI agent identity and authorization concept paper

title: Call for Participation in AI Agent Protocol Community Group
summary: W3C launched the AI Agent Protocol Community Group, proposed by Gaowei Chang and supported by four others, to develop open web protocols for agent discovery, identity and collaboration. Its scope covers discovery and capability exchange, an open-standards identity framework for cross-domain authentication, web-native agent metadata (capabilities, interfaces, goals, states) and security mechanisms such as verifiable credentials.
relevance: Standardized agent capability and state metadata on the web is a candidate substrate for describing and transferring agent tasks across domains.
search_query: W3C AI Agent Protocol Community Group launched
notes: Community Groups are not W3C standards-track; W3C does not endorse CG output.

title: Minutes — Agent Communication Protocols (agentproto) BoF
summary: At IETF 126, the working-group-forming agentproto BoF (chairs Leslie Daigle and Orie Steele, AD Charles Eckel) recorded non-binding show-of-hands results: 155-30 that interoperability is needed, 154-51 for forming a WG, but 38-124 against the initial scope as written. Participants proposed narrowing the charter, including reframing it around context propagation and a signaling protocol for managing context across trust boundaries; scope discussion moved to the mailing list.
relevance: The IETF is debating a standards-track home for agent communication, and one proposed framing (context propagation across trust boundaries) maps directly onto the portable-task-context problem.
search_query: IETF 126 agentproto BoF agent communication protocols outcome working group
notes: Minutes are marked draft for chair review; results are a sense of the room, to be confirmed on the mailing list. Secondary coverage: Forkast, 'IETF Bets on Agent Interoperability — But the Scope Fight Is Just Beginning' (2026-07-23), which reports the votes as a charter decision; treat that framing with caution.

title: IETF 126 Highlights
summary: The IETF's recap of its 126th meeting notes that three of the five BoFs concerned AI agent communication and coordination: DAWN (decentralized discovery, including agent-to-agent discovery), DMSC (a non-WG-forming diagnostic BoF on AI agent gateway models) and agentproto (agent communication building blocks and WG chartering). It points to continued mailing-list discussion rather than reporting outcomes.
relevance: Shows agent discovery, gateways and communication are now a major share of new IETF work, a signal for where interoperable handoff standards may land.
search_query: IETF 126 agentproto BoF agent communication protocols outcome working group
notes: The post states it was compiled from pre-meeting agendas, not session outcomes.

title: AI Agent Observability - Evolving Standards and Best Practices
summary: OpenTelemetry's GenAI SIG reported that a draft semantic convention for AI agent applications, based on Google's AI agent white paper, had been established, while a common convention for agent frameworks was still under discussion. The authors (IBM and Google) argued that standard telemetry shapes are needed to avoid lock-in to vendor- or framework-specific formats and contrasted baked-in framework instrumentation with OTel instrumentation libraries.
relevance: Framework-neutral agent telemetry is what lets a task's trace survive when the task moves across frameworks or runtimes.
search_query: opentelemetry.io blog AI agent observability evolving standards
notes: Publication date and authors taken from the post's source front matter in the opentelemetry.io GitHub repository; the rendered page does not display them.

title: Datadog Agent Observability natively supports OpenTelemetry GenAI Semantic Conventions
summary: Datadog announced that its LLM/agent observability product ingests spans following OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions v1.37 and later, via OTLP direct, the Datadog Agent or an OTel Collector. Datadog says GenAI attributes (model, provider, tokens, operation name) are mapped automatically, so teams no longer need its proprietary SDK for agent and tool traces.
relevance: Commercial adoption of the OTel GenAI conventions is evidence they are becoming the de facto cross-vendor format for agent traces.
search_query: Datadog native support OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions announcement
notes: Post title was later changed from 'Datadog LLM Observability natively supports...' to the current title.

title: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications – The Benchmark for Agentic Security in the Age of Autonomous AI
summary: OWASP's Agentic Security Initiative published its first Top 10 risk list for agentic applications (ASI01-ASI10), including agent goal hijack, tool misuse, identity and privilege abuse, memory and context poisoning, insecure inter-agent communication, cascading failures and rogue agents. It was launched at the London Agentic Security Summit and reviewed by an expert board with members from NIST, the Alan Turing Institute, Microsoft, AWS and others.
relevance: Context poisoning and insecure inter-agent communication are named top risks, which a portable task envelope and handoff protocol must explicitly mitigate.
search_query: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications released
notes: A press release on the same release is dated 2025-12-10.

title: NSA, partners release agentic AI guidance
technologies: Careful Adoption of Agentic AI Services
summary: Reports that on April 30, 2026 the NSA, Australia's ASD ACSC, Canada's Cyber Centre, CISA, New Zealand's NCSC and the UK NCSC published a joint Cybersecurity Information Sheet, 'Careful Adoption of Agentic AI Services'. The guidance groups agentic risks into privilege, design/configuration, behavior, structure and accountability, and recommends incremental deployment, least privilege, monitoring and human oversight.
relevance: Accountability and traceability across interconnected agents is a named government concern, directly relevant to preserving audit trails when tasks move between agents.
search_query: CISA NSA "Careful Adoption of Agentic AI Services" news
notes: Secondary source; the primary NSA/CISA advisory page was not fetched. Some sources date the release 2026-05-01.

title: Singapore Launches New Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI
publisher: Ministry of Digital Development and Information (MDDI), Singapore
technologies: Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI
summary: Minister Josephine Teo announced at the World Economic Forum in Davos an IMDA-developed Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI, building on Singapore's 2020 framework and aimed at organisations deploying in-house or third-party agents. It sets measures across four dimensions: bounding risk upfront (limiting autonomy and tool/data access), human approval at checkpoints, lifecycle technical controls, and end-user transparency and training.
relevance: A government framework that ties accountability to bounded agent permissions and checkpoints informs what governance metadata must travel with a delegated or migrated task.
search_query: IMDA "Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI" press release 22 January 2026 imda.gov.sg
notes: IMDA issued an updated version on 2026-05-20 (factsheet at imda.gov.sg) covering multi-agent and third-party agent risks; its body text could not be retrieved, so it is not listed separately.

title: New whitepaper tackles AI agent identity challenges
summary: The OpenID Foundation's AI Identity Management Community Group released the whitepaper 'Identity Management for Agentic AI' (arXiv:2510.25819). It finds current standards adequate for simple, single-domain agents but not designed for recursive delegation chains, cross-domain trust propagation or highly autonomous agents at scale, and recommends treating agents as first-class identities with lifecycle governance.
relevance: Recursive delegation and cross-domain trust propagation are exactly the identity problems raised when a task is handed across agents and organizations.
search_query: OpenID Foundation whitepaper identity management for agentic AI
